content.value_statement: Binary analysis findings can become scattered across triage, static, and dynamic notes. This skill turns verified evidence into concise reports, capability maps, and handoff summaries.
actual_capabilities: Reviews facts, hypotheses, and unresolved questions from previous analysis phases.
Correlates static findings, dynamic observations, strings, and behavior evidence.
Builds markdown reports with artifact details, capabilities, findings, and evidence logs.
Applies confidence labels to confirmed, refuted, uncertain, and unvalidated hypotheses.
Creates final knowledge journal entries for archival or handoff.
Suggests STIX-style threat intelligence formatting for potentially malicious binaries.
limitations: Does not execute binaries, inspect live systems, or collect evidence by itself.
Requires accurate notes from triage, static analysis, or dynamic analysis phases.
Cannot verify facts that are missing from the provided evidence.
STIX output still needs analyst review before external sharing.

use_cases.title: Prepare an analyst handoff
use_cases.description: Turn accumulated binary analysis notes into a report with evidence, confidence levels, and open questions.

use_cases.title: Close a reverse engineering case
use_cases.description: Validate hypotheses, document confirmed capabilities, and preserve final conclusions for future reference.

use_cases.title: Draft threat intelligence findings
use_cases.description: Summarize malicious capabilities, indicators, and uncertainty for review before intelligence sharing.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Use binary-re-synthesis to summarize these binary analysis notes. Separate confirmed findings, uncertain items, and remaining questions.

prompt_templates.title: Build a report
prompt_templates.prompt: Use binary-re-synthesis to create a binary analysis report with artifact details, capabilities, key functions, evidence, and recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Validate hypotheses
prompt_templates.prompt: Use binary-re-synthesis to evaluate each hypothesis against the evidence. Mark each as confirmed, refuted, uncertain, or unvalidated.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare intelligence summary
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced reporting for suspicious or malicious binaries.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use binary-re-synthesis to draft a threat intelligence summary with capabilities, evidence chains, confidence levels, and review notes.

output_examples.input: Analyst notes show a telemetry client with curl imports, a vendor URL string, and timed network submissions.
output_examples.output: A concise report states the primary purpose, supporting evidence, capability summary, confidence level, and unresolved payload questions.

output_examples.input: A hypothesis says the binary hosts a local web server, but no listener behavior was observed.
output_examples.output: The synthesis marks the hypothesis as refuted and explains that imports, calls, and runtime observations do not support server behavior.

output_examples.input: A suspicious sample needs final notes for threat intelligence review.
output_examples.output: The output lists observed capabilities, evidence sources, confidence labels, indicators to verify, and sharing cautions for analyst approval.

best_practices: Provide source notes with addresses, file paths, hashes, observations, and tool outputs.
Keep conclusions tied to evidence and label uncertainty clearly.
Review generated recommendations before sharing reports with stakeholders.
anti_patterns: Do not present speculation as a confirmed finding.
Do not omit contradictory evidence that weakens a hypothesis.
Do not use the skill as a substitute for collecting analysis evidence.

faq.question: Does this skill run or analyze binaries directly?
faq.answer: No. It synthesizes evidence that was already collected through other analysis steps.

faq.question: What input works best?
faq.answer: Use notes with hashes, architecture details, functions, strings, dynamic observations, hypotheses, and unresolved questions.

faq.question: Can it help with malware reports?
faq.answer: Yes. It can organize malicious capabilities, indicators, evidence chains, and analyst recommendations.

faq.question: How does it handle uncertainty?
faq.answer: It labels hypotheses as confirmed, refuted, uncertain, or unvalidated, then explains the evidence behind each status.

faq.question: Can it produce STIX-style summaries?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft threat intelligence summaries, but validated indicators are required before sharing.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
